newsitem.title: INDIA: Amnesty slams Indian forces for civilian deaths.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty slams Indian forces for civilian deaths.

text.p: Amnesty International on Tuesday accused India of allowing its security forces to kill civilians in the northeastern tribal state of Manipur.

"A pattern of apparently unlawful killings of suspected members of armed opposition groups has resulted from the systemic use of lethal force as an alternative to arrest by the security forces," the human rights group said.
Amnesty's report, made available to Reuters, examines the circumstances surrounding 14 deaths in 1995 and 1996, including those of women and children.
Indian government officials said they were unable to comment on the report.
"We haven't even seen this report," a government spokesman told Reuters. "When it comes, the government will see. At the moment I'm not able to say anything on it."
Since the 1950s, Indian authorities in the northeastern states have struggled to contain separatist uprisings by tribal groups seeking self-determination.
London-based Amnesty protested against Indian legislation in force in Manipur for the last four decades which it said gave the armed forces broadly defined powers to shoot to kill.

"The pattern of killings and the legislative context in which they take place leads Amnesty International to conclude that there is an official policy of sanction for extrajudicial executions in the region," the report said.
